intended_object: The free product of the groups underlying a family of profinite groups (G_i)_{i∈ι}, i.e. their coproduct ∗_i G_i in the category of groups, with the topology ignored. Inferred from the docstring ("abstract free product of the underlying groups") and the module documentation, where it is the group that gets completed to build the profinite free product.
explanation:
The body applies Mathlib's `Monoid.CoprodI` directly to the family of underlying monoids `(G i).group.toMonoid`. `Monoid.CoprodI` is Mathlib's free product (coproduct) of a family of monoids. When every factor is a group, Mathlib gives it a group instance, and it is then the usual free product of groups. The definition adds no conditions and changes nothing, so it is exactly the abstract free product of the underlying groups.

Being specialised to profinite groups is not a problem of generality. The definition is only a thin abbreviation that applies the general Mathlib construction to this family, so the library can refer to it while building the profinite free product. The verdict is faithful.
